questions.prompt: Two big reasons for social influence:
choices: A Only genetic mutation.
B Normative (be liked/avoid trouble) and informational (be right) motives.
C Only hunger.
D Ignoring all others.
questions.explain: Liked vs right—normative and informational influence.

choices: A People never conform on easy perceptual tasks.
B Group pressure can make people give wrong line judgments.
C Only experts are influenced.
D Conformity requires electric shocks.
questions.explain: Classic conformity: match the wrong line under group pressure.

choices: A Start tiny then huge with no retreat.
B Start with an extreme ask then retreat to a smaller request (Mexico week → smaller ask).
C Only foot-in-the-door.
D Never used by teens.
questions.explain: Big ask then smaller concession request.

choices: A Almost nobody continues to high shock levels.
B About two-thirds go to the XXX/450V range depending on setup—obedience is powerful.
C Only psychopaths obey.
D Isolation always reduces obedience to zero.
questions.explain: ~2/3 shock to max in classic setups.

choices: A Maximize isolation and FOMO via social media comparison.
B Get outside doing social stuff with people—isolation/loneliness/social media FOMO aren't helpful.
C Only online friends count.
D Never join groups.
questions.explain: Real-world social engagement over isolated FOMO.
